figure: FIGURE A.2 — A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
issue: The legend's first two entries are distinguished primarily by hue (brown vs blue) with border style as the only redundant cue; in grayscale the brown and blue swatches are close in luminance, so a grayscale reader must decode the legend by border style alone. The third entry (purple, thick) is separable, but the family boundary between 'efficiency-led' and 'capability-led' is not.
evidence: Legend swatches: brown with dashed border, blue with solid border, purple with thick border; the bands repeat the same three treatments.
acceptance_test: Grayscale conversion of the figure still lets a reader assign every band to a legend family without relying on hue (e.g. add a hatch or a left-edge marker to one family, or separate the families with a rule).

issue: The core distinction the figure encodes — 'blue = where the system runs' vs 'green = where the model runs' (the basis of the callout 'Model intelligence ≠ system intelligence') — is carried by hue only. In grayscale the two palettes overlap: the medium-blue band 'Inside agent runtime' and the medium-green band 'Inside attention' render at similar mid-grays, and the light-blue 'Inside tools' / light-green 'Inside weights' likewise. A print reader cannot map the legend's color words to the bands, so the system-vs-model split (the figure's main message) is lost. No non-color cue (border style, hatching, divider, or bracket) separates the two groups.
evidence: Legend line: 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs'. Bands 2–5 use a blue gradient, bands 6–8 a green gradient; all share the same solid-border style, so hue is the only group discriminator. The red left arrow and red callout box remain visible in grayscale, but they do not encode the blue/green split.
acceptance_test: Add a non-color cue separating the system group (top 5 bands) from the model group (bottom 3 bands) — e.g. a horizontal divider line with a small 'SYSTEM' / 'MODEL' bracket label on the left, or distinct border styles/hatching per group — and re-verify in a grayscale render that a reader can identify which bands are 'system' vs 'model' without using the color words in the legend.

issue: The color legend 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs' misclassifies 'Inside post-training' (and arguably 'Inside test-time search') as system-side, although post-training is a model-development/training activity and test-time search can be model-inference compute.
evidence: Legend: 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs'. Bands: 'Inside post-training' is blue; 'Inside test-time search' is blue; 'Inside weights/attention/MoE routing' are green.
acceptance_test: Recolor 'Inside post-training' as model-side or replace the binary legend with a three-way or explicit placement taxonomy (model internals / model development / system orchestration); ensure every band's color matches its stated definition.

figure: FIGURE A.3 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue: The figure's central semantic distinction — 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs' — is carried by hue alone. In grayscale the four blue bands and three green bands collapse into two overlapping luminance ramps, and the boundary between 'Inside test-time search' (blue, system) and 'Inside post-training' (green, model) becomes unreadable. That boundary is the figure's whole point.
evidence: In-figure note: 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs'. Bands: 'Across a fleet of models', 'Inside agent runtime', 'Inside tools', 'Inside test-time search' (blue family); 'Inside post-training', 'Inside MoE routing', 'Inside attention', 'Inside weights' (green family).
acceptance_test: A grayscale rendering of FIG A.3 still shows which side of the system/model boundary each band falls on — e.g. a horizontal rule plus a group label ('system-side' / 'model-side') at the boundary, or a hatch on one family; the hue note remains as a secondary cue.

issue: White labels on the light green 'Inside weights' and light blue 'Inside post-training' bands have low contrast, especially in grayscale, making those band labels harder to read at print size.
evidence: Rendered page: 'Inside weights' is white text on a light green fill; 'Inside post-training' is white text on a light blue fill. The fills are the lightest in the figure.
acceptance_test: Use dark text on light fills or darken the fills; verify WCAG contrast (at least 4.5:1 for normal text) and confirm legibility in a grayscale print proof.

figure: FIGURE A.3 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue: The figure draws a large upward red arrow labelled 'scope of placement: intelligence shifts up out of the weights', which encodes a directional, upward-is-more-advanced reading, while both the in-figure note and the caption insist the axis is 'not a ranking'. The drawn arrow is the strongest visual element on the page and it contradicts the stated semantics; a reader is likely to conclude 'up is better'.
evidence: In-figure note: 'scope of placement: intelligence shifts up out of the weights (vertical axis = WHERE it lives: nonexclusive placement choices, not a ranking)'. Caption: 'The horizontal bands are a design choice (which layer owns which capability), not a ranking of superiority; a lower band is not "better" or "worse" than a higher one'. Rendered: a single-headed red arrow rising from the 'Inside weights' band to the 'Across a fleet of models' band.
acceptance_test: The arrow is either made double-headed with a label that names it as an observed trend rather than a preference (e.g. 'observed direction of travel, not a recommendation'), or removed and replaced by a neutral axis marker; the caption's 'not a ranking' claim and the drawn geometry must be mutually consistent.

figure: FIGURE A.3 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue: Chapter references inside the figure use two different formats — a range with an en dash ('Ch 17–20') and a comma list ('Ch 19, Ch 24') — within the same right-hand column, and the range form is used only once. The reader cannot tell whether the difference is meaningful.
evidence: Right-hand labels: 'Ch 18, Ch 20'; 'Ch 17–20, Ch 24'; 'Ch 19, Ch 24'; 'Ch 8, Ch 20'; 'Ch 19, Ch 21'; 'Ch 10'; 'Ch 7, Ch 8'; 'Ch 3, Ch 8'.
acceptance_test: One format is used throughout the figure (e.g. 'Ch 17, Ch 18, Ch 19, Ch 20, Ch 24'), and the same format is used in the book's other figure-embedded chapter references.

figure: FIGURE A.3 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue: The arrow's explanatory text is set in small red type, centered under the band stack and detached from the arrow it describes, while the arrow itself carries no label. The reader's eye enters at the arrow (the only saturated element) and finds no text attached to it.
evidence: Rendered: a red vertical arrow at the far left with no adjacent label; the red note 'scope of placement: intelligence shifts up out of the weights (vertical axis = WHERE it lives: nonexclusive placement choices, not a ranking)' sits below the bands, centered, in small type.
acceptance_test: The arrow carries its label adjacent to the shaft (rotated or in a short callout), and the note is set at the same size as the other in-figure annotations.

figure: Figure A.4 (Shared weights do not remove executed work), 'Actual stop' row
issue: In the 'Actual stop' row the solid flow line from 'pass 2' appears to enter the dashed 'pass 3 (not executed)' box and then continue to 'exit', visually placing the not-executed step on the execution path. This contradicts the 'not executed' label, the legend ('dashed box = not executed'), and the figure's purpose (an early exit removes pass 3's work). A reader can plausibly infer that pass 3 runs, which is the opposite of the intended contrast with the 'Post-hoc selection' row (where all three passes run).
evidence: Rendered 'Actual stop' row: pass 1 → pass 2, then a solid line/arrow into the dashed 'pass 3' box (captioned 'not executed'), then a solid arrow to the tan 'exit' box. Compare 'Post-hoc selection' row where pass 3 is a solid (executed) box. Legend: 'Solid arrows = flow; dashed box = not executed.'
acceptance_test: Redraw the 'Actual stop' row so the solid flow arrow goes directly from 'pass 2' to 'exit'; the dashed 'pass 3' box must carry no incoming flow arrow (show it as a skipped/omitted element, e.g. a bypass line over it or a 'skipped' tag). At print size a reader must not be able to infer that pass 3 executes on the actual-stop path.

issue: In the 'Actual stop' path, a solid flow arrow runs from pass 2 into the dashed 'pass 3 not executed' box, while the actual exit is a separate orange arrow from pass 2 to exit. The mixed solid-arrow-into-dashed-box encoding makes the reading order ambiguous.
evidence: Figure: 'Actual stop' row shows pass 1 → pass 2 → dashed box 'pass 3 not executed' → exit, plus an orange arrow from pass 2 to exit. Legend: 'dashed box = not executed; Solid arrows = flow'.
acceptance_test: Remove the solid arrow into the dashed box or make that arrow dashed/ghosted; route the actual exit arrow directly from pass 2 to exit and place the dashed 'not executed' box off the flow path.

figure: FIGURE A.4 — Shared-depth execution reuses weights, not necessarily history state
issue: In the 'Exit after pass 2' row, the solid orange arrow to the 'exit' box originates from the dashed 'pass 3' box that is explicitly labelled 'not executed'. The drawn geometry therefore shows the exit occurring after pass 3's slot, directly contradicting the row heading 'Exit after pass 2' and the caption's 'A true exit omits later work'. A reader can infer that the exit happens after pass 3 — the opposite of the figure's point.
evidence: Rendered row 1: 'pass 1 → pass 2 → [pass 3, dashed, 'not executed'] → exit', with a solid orange arrow from the dashed pass-3 box to the orange 'exit' box. Row heading: 'Exit after pass 2: two different runtime paths'. Caption: 'A true exit omits later work; selecting an earlier representation after all passes does not.'
acceptance_test: The exit arrow originates from 'pass 2' (the last executed pass), or the pass-3→exit connector is drawn dashed and the exit box is labelled 'exit (after pass 2)'; no solid flow arrow may leave a box marked 'not executed'.

issue: In the upper diagram, the 'one shared core weight set' box appears to connect by dashed weight-reuse arrows to pass 1 and pass 3 only; no dashed arrow to pass 2 is visible. If pass 2 lacks the weight-reuse arrow, the diagram contradicts its own title ('Shared-depth execution reuses weights') and the legend ('Dashed arrows = weight reuse'), implying that the middle pass does not use the shared weights.

figure: FIGURE A.4 — Shared-depth execution reuses weights, not necessarily history state
issue: The smallest in-figure text — the 'not executed' annotation under the dashed pass-3 box and the two-line legend ('Dashed arrows = weight reuse; dashed box = not executed. Illustrative exit index; no latency or quality result.') — is set below the size of the other annotations and is at risk of falling under the 8 pt print floor.
